title: Ere Mountains Reared Their Forms Sublime
description: Ere Mountains Reared Their Forms Sublime in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 107 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Eternity of God”, where the book credits them to the Spirit of the Psalms.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ere moun-tains reared their forms sub-lime, Or heaven and earth in or-der stood, Be-fore the birth of an-cient time, From ev-er-last-ing thou art God.

lines: Ere mountains reared their forms sublime,
Or heaven and earth in order stood,
Before the birth of ancient time,
A thousand ages, in their flight,
With thee are as a fleeting day;
Past, present, future, to thy sight
At once their various scenes display.
But our brief life's a shadowy dream,
A passing thought, that soon is o'er,
That fades with morning's earliest beam,
And fills the musing mind no more.
To us, O Lord, the wisdom give,
Each passing moment so to spend,
That we at length with thee may live
Where life and bliss shall never end.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
